paper_title: Aerobic oxidation and EATA-based highly enantioselective synthesis of lamenallenic acid†

questions.question: In this paper, what does the abbreviation 'EATA' stand for?
questions.ground_truth_answer: EATA = enantioselective allenylation of terminal alkynes.

questions.question: What IUPAC/common name is assigned in the paper to compound 25?
According to the paper's standard EATA reaction conditions (Table 1 and footnote), which solvent and temperature were used for the reaction?
questions.ground_truth_answer: The standard EATA conditions used dioxane as solvent at 130 °C in a sealed tube (reaction run 12 h).

questions.question: Which gave the higher NMR yield in Table 1: the reaction with R = Ph (entry 1) or the reaction with R = Me (entry 8)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: R = Me (entry 8) gave the higher NMR yield: 55% (entry 8) vs 52% for R = Ph (entry 1).

questions.question: What yield and E/Z ratio were reported for the isolated (−)-lamenallenic acid (Ra)-(−)-1 after hydrolysis (KOH)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: (−)-lamenallenic acid (Ra)-(−)-1 was obtained in 98% yield with E/Z = 94/6 (reported [α]D20 = −55.2, c = 0.995, EtOH).
